name: Launch Bay
summary: Hostile leper gnomes and corrupted machines hold Launch Bay beyond the Hall of Gears. Once Gnomeregan’s airfield for flying machines and bombers, this hangar lies deep beneath the city.

sections.title: A Grounded Airfield
sections.body:
Two tiers once held Gnomeregan’s aerial fleet. Ramps from the upper walkway lead to a central platform, where flying machines and heavy bombers remain parked. They were left behind before the city was evacuated.

Crazed leper gnomes now roam the flight decks. They maintain and guard the idle war machines where skilled pilots once served.

sections.title: Crossroads of the Deep City
sections.body:
Launch Bay joins several parts of the complex. Ramps from its southeastern corridor descend into the Engineering Labs.

On the lower deck, invading Dark Iron dwarves choke the southern passage. That tunnel offers a perilous route toward Tinkers' Court, deep in the city.

faq.q: What is the Launch Bay used for?
faq.answer: Launch Bay was built as an underground airfield and hangar for gnomish flying machines and bombers. Leper gnomes dwelling in the ruins have now taken over the neglected space.

faq.q: Who controls the Launch Bay now?
faq.answer: Leper gnomes and aggressive mechanical contraptions occupy Launch Bay’s upper and lower levels. Hostile Dark Iron dwarves have also carved out a foothold near the southern exits.

faq.q: Where does the Launch Bay lead?
faq.answer: The upper eastern tunnel leads back to the Hall of Gears. Southeastern ramps descend to the Engineering Labs, while a southern tunnel on the lower deck leads deeper into Gnomeregan toward Tinkers' Court.

faq.q: Are the flying machines here operational?
faq.answer: Several gnomish flying machines and bombers remain parked on the central platforms. They sit idle and untended amid the chaos of the city’s fall.

angles.text: As a gnome, seeing flying machines and bombers abandoned and overrun by irradiated leper kin is a bitter reminder of your city’s tragic loss.
As an engineer, you can see the hangar’s gnomish aeronautics and vehicle chassis up close, though hostile contraptions guard the area.
